tex_content.html:
Corollary
↗ prop:existence-uniqueness-jacobi-fields 1. ch10:10.3

If $(M,g)$ has dimension $n$ and $\gamma $ is any geodesic, then $\mathfrak J(\gamma )$ is a $2n$-dimensional linear space.

Proof

\sketch The Jacobi equation is linear. Evaluation at any $a\in I$ defines

\[ \mathfrak J(\gamma )\longrightarrow T_{\gamma (a)}M\oplus T_{\gamma (a)}M, \qquad J\longmapsto (J(a),D_tJ(a)), \]

which is an isomorphism by the preceding proposition.

□
